quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in -ed as [t] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'walked' and 'watched' end in [t], not [ɪd]. Neither gains a syllable.
quests.explanation: After a voiceless sound like [k] or [tʃ], -ed is a quick [t]. Say 'walk' and 'watch', then add a light tongue tap.
quests.textToSpeak: We walked to the harbour and watched the boats come in.
quests.phoneticHint: 'walked' [wɔːkt] and 'watched' [wɒtʃt] are one syllable each. The [kt] and [tʃt] endings are short.
commonMistakes: Dropping the final [t], so 'walked' sounds like 'walk'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would describe your morning.
quests.hint: 'stopped', 'picked' and 'rushed' all end in [t]: after [p], [k] and [ʃ].
quests.explanation: Voiceless [p], [k] and [ʃ] are followed by [t], so the consonants group together without a vowel. In connected speech, the [t] is light.
quests.textToSpeak: I stopped at the pharmacy, picked up my prescription, and rushed to work.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a tech story.
quests.hint: 'crashed' ends in [ʃt], 'switched' in [tʃt], and 'checked' in [kt].
quests.explanation: 'switched' has [tʃ] followed by [t]: hold the tongue on the ridge a little longer, then release. Don't add a vowel.
quests.textToSpeak: The app crashed twice, so I switched phones and checked again.

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in -ed as [d] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'called', 'answered' and 'emailed' end in [d] after voiced sounds. No extra syllable.
quests.explanation: After voiced sounds like [l] and [r], -ed becomes a light [d]. Keep the voice on right up to the end.
quests.textToSpeak: I called twice, but nobody answered, so I emailed instead.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a frustrated customer.
quests.hint: 'opened' ends in [nd] and 'moved' ends in [vd].
quests.explanation: After [n], the tongue stays on the ridge for [d]. After [v], the lip-teeth contact is released into a quick voiced [d].
quests.textToSpeak: The shop opened late, and the queue moved slowly.
quests.phoneticHint: 'opened' is [ˈoʊpənd], with two syllables; 'moved' is [muːvd], with one.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a travel story.
quests.hint: 'arrived' ends in [vd], 'changed' in [dʒd], and 'used' in [zd].
quests.explanation: Each ends with a voiced fricative or affricate followed by a light [d]. Keep the buzz through both sounds.
quests.textToSpeak: My train arrived early, so I changed my plans and used the tram.

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in -ed as [ɪd] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'wanted' and 'needed' add an extra syllable [ɪd] because the base verbs end in [t] or [d].
quests.explanation: When the verb already ends in [t] or [d], -ed adds a full syllable [ɪd]. Without it, the listener hears the present tense.
quests.textToSpeak: They wanted to finish early, but the buyer needed more time.
quests.phoneticHint: 'wanted' is [ˈwɒntɪd] and 'needed' is [ˈniːdɪd]: two syllables each.
commonMistakes: Saying 'wanted' as 'want' with no extra syllable
Making the ending [ed] with a full vowel

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a story about waiting.
quests.hint: 'waited' and 'started' both end with the syllable [ɪd].
quests.explanation: Give the ending its own beat, but keep it weak and short. The stressed first syllable carries the word.
quests.textToSpeak: We waited for ages, and then the concert started.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a story about moving house.
quests.hint: 'painted' and 'decorated' end with [ɪd]; 'landlord' has [ndl] inside it.
quests.explanation: 'decorated' has four syllables with stress on the first: [ˈdekəreɪtɪd]. The last syllable stays weak.
quests.textToSpeak: My landlord painted the hallway, and I decorated the bedroom.
commonMistakes: Saying 'decorated' as 'decorate' by dropping the ending

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in -ed: [t], [ɪd], [d] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'stopped' and 'looked' end in [t], 'decided' ends in [ɪd], and 'turned' ends in [d].
quests.explanation: Choose the ending by the last sound of the verb: voiceless gives [t], voiced gives [d], and [t] or [d] gives [ɪd].
quests.textToSpeak: I stopped, looked at the map, decided I was lost, and turned around.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a personal update.
quests.hint: 'tired' ends in [d], 'stressed' ends in [st], and 'excited' ends in [ɪd].
quests.explanation: Adjectives made from verbs follow the same -ed rules. 'excited' keeps its extra syllable because the base ends in [t].
quests.textToSpeak: I felt tired and stressed, but my sister was excited about the trip.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a personal update Watch the 'used to' and 'supposed to'.
quests.hint: 'used to' and 'supposed to' end in [t] before 'to', not [d].
quests.explanation: In these fixed phrases, the -ed sounds like [t] because the next word begins with [t]. The words blend into one unit.
quests.textToSpeak: I used to live near the office, but I'm supposed to relocate next year.
quests.phoneticHint: 'used to' is [juːst tə] and 'supposed to' is [səˈpoʊst tə].
commonMistakes: Saying 'used' as 'yoozd' with a full [z] and [d]

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in final [nθs] and [sts] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'months' ends in [nθs] and 'tests' ends in [sts]. 'six' ends in [ks].
quests.explanation: Say 'month' first: [n] then [θ]. Add [s] with the tongue still near the teeth. For 'tests', hiss, tap and hiss without any vowels.
quests.textToSpeak: It took nearly six months to pass all the tests.
commonMistakes: Dropping the middle [t] in 'tests', so it sounds like 'tess'

quests.instruction: Say it twice: first carefully, then at natural speed, keeping final [ksts] and [fts] intact.
quests.hint: 'texts' ends in [ksts] and 'gifts' ends in [fts].
quests.explanation: Move the tongue quickly through each consonant: [k], [s], [t], [s]. In casual speech many people simplify 'texts', but practise the full form first.
quests.textToSpeak: I got your texts; I'll send the gifts on Friday.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an interview answer.
quests.hint: 'strengths' ends in [ŋθs]; 'weaknesses' ends in [ɪz].
quests.explanation: 'strengths' has [str], then [e], then [ŋ], [θ] and [s]. Keep the back of the tongue up for [ŋ], then move forward to the teeth for [θ].
quests.textToSpeak: In interviews, I explain my strengths first and my weaknesses last.

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in [lk] and [lm] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: 'milk' ends in [lk] and 'film' ends in [lm]. Keep the [l] before the last sound.
quests.explanation: For [lk], the tongue tip stays on the ridge for [l] while the back lifts for [k]. For [lm], finish [l], then close the lips for [m].
quests.textToSpeak: We ran out of milk, so I'll pick some up after the film.
quests.phoneticHint: 'milk' is [mɪlk], one syllable; 'film' is [fɪlm], one syllable.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a request for help.
quests.hint: 'help' ends in [lp], and 'myself' ends in [lf].
quests.explanation: Keep the tongue tip on the ridge for [l], then release it as the lips close for [p]. For [lf], the lip-teeth hiss follows the [l].
quests.textToSpeak: I could use some help; I can't do it by myself.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a health update Watch the [lθ] and [lf].
quests.hint: 'health' ends in [lθ] and 'golf' ends in [lf].
quests.explanation: After [l], the tongue tip moves forward to the teeth for [θ]. For 'golf', the lip goes to the teeth after the [l].
quests.textToSpeak: My health has improved since I started playing golf.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a reaction to news.
quests.hint: 'exactly' has [ktl] in the middle; 'government' has [rnm].
quests.explanation: Don't insert vowels: 'exactly' is [ɪgˈzæktli], with [kt] then [l]. In 'government', the [n] and [m] come together quickly.
quests.textToSpeak: That's exactly what the government promised last year.
commonMistakes: Dropping the [t] in 'exactly', so it sounds like 'exackly'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as travel news.
quests.hint: 'postpone' has [stp] in the middle, 'transport' has [nsp], and 'strike' begins with [str].
quests.explanation: Keep every consonant: 'postpone' is [poʊst] then [poʊn]. In 'transport', the [n] flows into [s] and then [p].
quests.textToSpeak: We had to postpone the trip because of a transport strike.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a lost-property report.
quests.hint: 'handbag' has [ndb], 'platform' has [tf], and 'handed' has [ndɪd].
quests.explanation: In 'handbag', say [n], then move straight to [d] and [b] without a pause. In 'platform', the [t] stops the air right before the [f].
quests.textToSpeak: Someone left a handbag on the platform, so I handed it to the guard.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a report on failed calls.
quests.hint: 'attempts' ends in [mpts] and 'contact' has [ntækt].
quests.explanation: Keep the lips closed for [mp] and release into [t] and [s] quickly. In 'contact', the tongue flows from [n] to [t] to [k].
quests.textToSpeak: They made three attempts to contact us, but nothing worked.
quests.phoneticHint: 'attempts' is [əˈtempts] and 'contact' is [ˈkɒntækt]. Don't add a vowel between the sounds.
commonMistakes: Saying 'contact' as 'contac' by dropping the last [t]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a warning Watch the [sts] and [kts].
quests.hint: 'costs' ends in [sts]; 'contracts' ends in [kts].
quests.explanation: 'costs' has hiss, tap, hiss; 'contracts' has stop, tap, hiss. Practise each ending slowly before saying the sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: The costs are in the contracts, so read the small print before you sign.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as workplace advice.
quests.hint: 'directly' contains [ktl]; 'plainly' contains [nl].
quests.explanation: In 'directly', [k] and [t] come together, then [l]. Release the [k] almost silently, tap [t], and go straight into [l]. In 'plainly', the tongue tip stays on the ridge from [n] to [l].
quests.textToSpeak: Speak directly to the supervisor and say plainly what went wrong.

quests.instruction: Read it slowly so every consonant in final [p] and [b] is heard, then at normal speed.
quests.hint: Both 'tap' and 'tub' end in a stop: close the lips and stop, with no vowel after.
quests.explanation: Close both lips to end the word and hold the air. Don't release with a puff or add [ə]. The vowel before [b] is slightly longer.
quests.textToSpeak: Turn the tap off before the tub overflows.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a story about a school result.
quests.hint: 'mad', 'bad' and 'grade' end in [d].
quests.explanation: Keep the tongue on the ridge and the voice on until the closure. The vowel is longer before [d] than before [t].
quests.textToSpeak: He was mad about the bad grade, but he didn't argue.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a trip description.
quests.hint: 'big' ends in [g], 'lake' in [k], and 'ridge' in [dʒ].
quests.explanation: Each ends with a closure at a different place: back of the tongue for [g] and [k], blade against the ridge for [dʒ]. Hold and stop cleanly.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a big lake, and the trail along the ridge is the best part.
commonMistakes: Devoicing the final [g], so 'big' sounds like 'bik'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a manager's note.
quests.hint: Watch [rts] in 'starts', [nθ] in 'month', [sts] in 'costs', [vd] in 'approved', and [rst] in 'first'.
quests.explanation: Keep every consonant but add no extra vowels. The final clusters carry the meaning: 'starts', 'costs' and 'approved'.
quests.textToSpeak: Just so you know, the project starts next month, and all costs must be approved first.
quests.phoneticHint: 'starts' is [stɑːrts], 'month' is [mʌnθ], 'costs' is [kɒsts], 'approved' is [əˈpruːvd], and 'first' is [fɜːrst].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a story from a dinner out.
quests.hint: 'asked' ends in [kt]; 'restaurant' has [str]; 'booked' ends in [kt]; 'waited' ends in [ɪd].
quests.explanation: Two of the -ed endings are [t] and one is [ɪd]. 'restaurant' is often said in two syllables: [ˈrestrɒnt].
quests.textToSpeak: We asked for a quiet table, but the restaurant was fully booked, so we waited.
quests.phoneticHint: 'asked' is [æskt], 'restaurant' is [ˈrestrɒnt] or [ˈrestərɒnt], 'booked' is [bʊkt], and 'waited' is [ˈweɪtɪd].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a workplace update.
quests.hint: 'texted' has [kstɪd]; 'slipped' ends in [pt]; 'explained' has [nd]; 'risks' ends in [sks]; 'asked' ends in [kt].
quests.explanation: Pay attention to each ending: only 'texted' adds a syllable; 'slipped', 'explained' and 'asked' don't. 'risks' has three consonants at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: The schedule slipped, so I texted the supplier, explained the risks, and asked for more time.
